meanings.note: Comparative of много. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('old-fashioned').

examples.trans: No, this is my grandfather's antique.

держаться.gloss: to hold on; to stick with

meanings.note: за + accusative: держись за руку = hold on to my hand

meanings.en: to stick with, keep close to
meanings.note: + genitive: держитесь меня = stick with me

Держись! = hang in there!. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hold on; to stick with'.

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Stick with me and everything will be fine.

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё у вас будет хорошо. Потому что я кто?
examples.trans: Stick with me, and everything will be fine for you. Because who am I?

meanings.note: About people. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind; good').
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters

meanings.note: Singular only. Common feminine noun meaning 'food, meal' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Elderly man. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тарик'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'old man' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This old man is sitting on the bench.
The old man told an interesting story.
